questions.q: The article says a list of real needs ends in a full stop, but a wish-list has “only commas.” What follows from this?
options: We should write down our wishes and meet them one by one
Not quite. The article says: Happiness comes from contentment, not abundance, because desires never end.
Happiness comes from contentment, not abundance, because desires never end
Yes. “Happiness is not a destination; it is a state of mind.”
Happiness requires giving up all possessions
Not quite. The article says: Happiness comes from contentment, not abundance, because desires never end.
Needs and desires are really the same
Not quite. The article says: Happiness comes from contentment, not abundance, because desires never end.
questions.rationale: “There is always a full-stop in the list of real needs, but the wish-list based on desire has no full-stop… it is only contentment that can give you happiness, not abundance.”

questions.q: What practical benefit of contentment does the author describe from his own life?
options: Fewer responsibilities
Not quite. The article says: Freedom from distraction, leaving time for study, positive thinking and service.
Freedom from distraction, leaving time for study, positive thinking and service
Right. A happy person is free of tension.
More wealth than he expected
Not quite. The article says: Freedom from distraction, leaving time for study, positive thinking and service.
Fame among his readers
Not quite. The article says: Freedom from distraction, leaving time for study, positive thinking and service.
questions.rationale: “This contentment has saved me from all kinds of distractions. And when you are saved from distractions, you have enough time to do all kinds of good things.”

questions.q: Stars and planets move constantly yet never collide. What lesson does the article take from them?
options: To avoid all movement and change
Not quite. The article says: To pursue our own aims without coming into conflict with others.
To keep far away from other people
Not quite. The article says: To pursue our own aims without coming into conflict with others.
To pursue our own aims without coming into conflict with others
Yes. Nature knows only positivity.
To follow whoever is strongest
Not quite. The article says: To pursue our own aims without coming into conflict with others.
questions.rationale: “This shows us how to proceed to our destination in life without coming into conflict with others.”

questions.q: Mandela’s and Gandhi’s recorded speeches are still heard after their deaths. What argument does the article build on this?
options: Only famous people are remembered
Not quite. The article says: If one part of the personality – the voice – survives, the whole personality can survive too.
Great leaders never really die in people’s hearts
Not quite. The article says: If one part of the personality – the voice – survives, the whole personality can survive too.
If one part of the personality – the voice – survives, the whole personality can survive too
Well reasoned. The Quran says it is “as true as your ability to speak.”
Technology will one day end death
Not quite. The article says: If one part of the personality – the voice – survives, the whole personality can survive too.
questions.rationale: “If a part of our personality is alive after our physical death, why cannot our whole personality be alive after our death?”

questions.q: The article notes that the body’s cells are wholly replaced about every ten years. What does it infer?
options: The body is more lasting than the mind
Not quite. The article says: The personality stays the same through these changes, so it need not end with the body’s final death.
The personality stays the same through these changes, so it need not end with the body’s final death
Exactly. “Personality is changelessness in change.”
A person becomes someone new every ten years
Not quite. The article says: The personality stays the same through these changes, so it need not end with the body’s final death.
Ageing can be prevented
Not quite. The article says: The personality stays the same through these changes, so it need not end with the body’s final death.
questions.rationale: “If in spite of nine ‘deaths’, the personality has remained intact, then why must it die when the physical body dies the tenth and final time?”

questions.q: The article calls the demand for job reservations a kind of shortcut. What does it say truly lifts a community?
options: Stronger political leaders
Not quite. The article says: Becoming able to meet competition and challenge.
Living apart from other communities
Not quite. The article says: Becoming able to meet competition and challenge.
Larger grants from government
Not quite. The article says: Becoming able to meet competition and challenge.
Becoming able to meet competition and challenge
Correct. Favours “only paralyse its abilities.”
questions.rationale: “No amount of favours can uplift any community. The only way to empower a community is to make it capable of meeting the challenges that it faces.”

questions.q: What does a “ROAD CLOSED” sign teach about life, according to the article?
options: When the direct way is blocked there are other routes, even if slower and less direct
Yes. They are open to those with “the eyes to see” and the courage to take them.
One should wait until the road reopens
Not quite. The article says: When the direct way is blocked there are other routes, even if slower and less direct.
A closed road means the journey should be given up
Not quite. The article says: When the direct way is blocked there are other routes, even if slower and less direct.
Obstacles should be removed by force
Not quite. The article says: When the direct way is blocked there are other routes, even if slower and less direct.
questions.rationale: “For every major route which is blocked, there are always several minor roads that are open… For every closed door, there is always another which is open.”

questions.q: How does human growth differ from the growth of a seed into a tree?
options: A seed grows automatically; a person must develop himself by conscious effort
Right. Potential is given by nature; unfolding it is our own task.
A seed needs care; a person grows untended
Not quite. The article says: A seed grows automatically; a person must develop himself by conscious effort.
A seed grows slowly; a person at once
Not quite. The article says: A seed grows automatically; a person must develop himself by conscious effort.
A seed has little potential; a person has none at birth
Not quite. The article says: A seed grows automatically; a person must develop himself by conscious effort.
questions.rationale: “A seed grows automatically, following the law of nature. Man however, is required to develop his personality by his own efforts.”

questions.q: A tree takes food from soil, water, air and light. What is the parallel for a person?
options: Reading books on every subject
Not quite. The article says: Drawing lessons and strength from every situation, including unwanted and negative ones.
Seeking the company of every kind of person
Not quite. The article says: Drawing lessons and strength from every situation, including unwanted and negative ones.
Drawing lessons and strength from every situation, including unwanted and negative ones
Well read. Controlling anger, for instance, builds the art of turning negative into positive.
Avoiding hardship so as to grow in peace
Not quite. The article says: Drawing lessons and strength from every situation, including unwanted and negative ones.
questions.rationale: “We must extract this nourishment for our development from all things, including negative things, and unwanted situations.”

questions.q: The Prophet compared the five daily prayers to a stream at one’s door in which one bathes five times a day. What did he mean?
options: Prayer must be preceded by a full bath
Not quite. The article says: As bathing leaves no dirt on the body, the prayers wash away minor sins.
Prayer is best offered beside water
Not quite. The article says: As bathing leaves no dirt on the body, the prayers wash away minor sins.
As bathing leaves no dirt on the body, the prayers wash away minor sins
Yes. Prayer said in its true spirit keeps one from indecency and evil.
Prayer is as easy as bathing
Not quite. The article says: As bathing leaves no dirt on the body, the prayers wash away minor sins.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet then explained that, in the same manner, the five daily prayers as ordered by God will erase all minor sins.”
